discovery: Conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC, enabling the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, 'recently confirmed through the discovery of the predicted fundamental particle by the ATLAS and CMS experiments'. The discovery itself was made possible by detectors of unprecedented scale and precision, whose concepts were championed from the late 1980s by Della Negra and Virdee (CMS) and Jenni (ATLAS). Their designs - a compact high-field solenoid with crystal electromagnetic calorimetry and all-silicon tracking for CMS, and the large toroidal muon spectrometer with liquid-argon calorimetry for ATLAS - were optimised precisely for the H->gamma-gamma and H->ZZ->4-lepton channels that revealed the 125 GeV boson in 2012. They led these projects from conception through construction and early physics, establishing instruments that continue to measure Higgs couplings and probe physics beyond the Standard Model. Their work demonstrates that visionary instrumentation is itself a fundamental discovery in physics.
